raj: Heads up — noticed a ~4% spike in invoice_preview token counts this morning tied to a commit-window surge between 03:10-03:14 UTC. Looks correlated with the new header normalization change rolled last night.
maria: ack. Which header exactly? the X-Route or the new x-client-id-canonicalization?
raj: x-client-id-canonicalization. Some proxies were normalizing to lowercase and we ended up double-counting when both original and normalized headers arrived in the ingest fanout.
sam: double-counting how? duplicate routing keys or different fingerprinting flow?
jin: The pipeline dedupe uses route_fingerprint = sha(route_header || tenant_id). If two different header variants make it through before dedupe window expires, they're seen as separate sessions.
emily: That explains the invoice preview bump. Any idea how many tenants hit this vs system-wide?
aj: Rough sample: ~120 tenants had +3-20% temporary delta; majority on legacy proxies. The surge coincided with a batch commit on aggregator that widened the commit window from 30s -> 3m (unintended rollout flag).
maria: Oof. So two failures combined: header normalization + extended commit window. What immediate mitigation can we do that doesn't require a full rollback?
sam: Short-term: reduce commit window back to 30s (config flag rollback). Also add a transient normalization dedupe step at ingress that canonicalizes header variants before fingerprinting.
jin: I can push a lightweight normalization transform in the sidecar (lowercase + trim). That should collapse both variants into a single fingerprint.
emily: Will that require backfilling invoices or just stop future double-counts?
aj: It stops future doubles. For already-previewed invoices we need a reconciliation run to mark which previews were inflated. We should not auto-charge customers until we reconcile.
maria: Action items:
- sam: rollback commit window (quick config toggle)
- jin: push sidecar header canonicalization (canary on 10% of edge)
- raj + emily: run diff job for previews and mark affected invoice previews as "under review"
- deploy-bot: create alert for sudden preview token delta (>2% over baseline)
sam: I'll flip the commit-window flag now.
(2m later)
sam: done. commit_window reverted to 30s on edge-prod cluster. monitoring shows acked commits back to baseline.
jin: prepping sidecar change. Quick note on implementation:
```
# nginx / envoy style canonicalization
set $client_id $http_x_client_id;
# prefer snake -> lower, strip spaces
client_id_norm = strtolower(trim($client_id));
# ensure single header passed to ingest
proxy_set_header X-Client-Id-Norm $client_id_norm;
```
I'll push a canary to 3 nodes in eu-west first.
maria: Please include unit test for header variants and an integration test verifying fingerprint dedupe within a 5s window.
jin: will do.
raj: For the backfill/reconciliation: I'll run a sampling job that recomputes route_fingerprint using normalized headers for the window 03:00-04:00 and produce a per-tenant delta table. Emily, can your billing script ingest a list of affected invoice_preview ids to flag for manual review?
emily: yes. If you can output CSV: tenant_id, preview_id, delta_tokens, earliest_event_ts — we'll enqueue into billing-review queue.
aj: ok. I already kicked off a job, ETA ~40m. Output will be in s3://billing-audit/preview-deltas/7054321987-delta.csv
sam: We should also consider hardening dedupe logic: make fingerprinting robust to header variants and add a short-lived global idempotency token when requests pass the edge.
maria: Agreed. Two medium-term engineering solutions:
1) canonicalize headers at edge AND make fingerprinting tolerant (normalization + stable hashing)
2) emit and persist an idempotency token for session creation (so duplicates within T window map back)
jin: idempotency token needs to be propagated end-to-end and cheap. Maybe a stable hash of tenant_id + timestamp_bucket + canonical_client_id?
sam: I'd prefer a real random UUID on creation, but that would require callers to pass it. Not feasible for every existing client quickly.
emily: For billing audit we only need deterministic collision-free keys for same-session grouping. Hash approach sounds ok.
raj: Let's pragmatic-ship: implement canonicalization + normalization hashing this sprint. Follow-up PR for idempotency token in next sprint.
maria: Can we also add an ingest-side metric: unique_fingerprint_ratio and raw_header_variants_count — so ops can spot regressions early?
aj: Good idea — I'll add instrumentation in the dedupe service.
deploy-bot: deploy request created by jin: canary sidecar header-normalization -> 3 nodes in eu-west. change-id: CHG-9981
jin: canary live. initial telemetry shows raw_header_variants_count down 92% on canary nodes.
sam: Nice. Once we have stable metrics for 10m without regressions, roll to 50% then 100%.
jin: rolling. ETA full roll ~25m.
emily: Keep me updated on the CSV. We need to freeze invoices for the affected preview window until audit done.
raj: CSV will be ready in ~30m, starting diff run now.
maria: Postmortem notes: root cause = simultaneous rollout of normalization change + widen commit window flag. We need a rollout checklist: any normalization-involving change must be canaried and paired with commit-window change approvals.
sam: also add an automated integration test for commit_window config change that runs on staging to ensure commit ack latency and dedupe invariants.
aj: I'll add to the rollout playbook and file a ticket: RB-215 (rollout checklist + staging gating)
maria: thanks everyone. Once audit CSV is in S3, Emily/Raj can coordinate next steps on billing review. If any tenant disputes come in, route to billing-review channel.
emily: will do. Thanks for the quick responses :thumbsup:
raj: preemptive note: will follow up with a small dashboard card showing "preview-token-delta" and a link to the audit CSV.
maria: closing thread once CSV + canary full roll done. moving to postmortem doc later.
deploy-bot: commit_window flag toggled by sam at 7054322060. canary deploy CHG-9981 started at 7054322810.
